question.text:
CASE STUDY (Continued): Mr. Sharma's investments: Investment 1: Equity MF - LTCG Rs. 3,00,000 (held 15 months) Investment 2: Debt MF - purchased Feb 2024, gain Rs. 50,000 (held 8 months) Investment 3: ELSS - LTCG Rs. 80,000 (held 4 years) Investment 4: IDCW of Rs. 8,000 received
Question 4: What is Mr. Sharma's TOTAL tax liability across ALL four mutual fund components including 4% cess?

answer.text: Rs. 41,080 (using old LTCG rate of 10% for equity and old Rs. 1 lakh exemption)
Rs. 51,246 (Equity LTCG: Rs. 22,750 + Debt: Rs. 15,600 + ELSS LTCG: Rs. 10,400 + IDCW: Rs. 2,496)
Rs. 50,446 (incorrectly netting TDS of Rs. 800 from total tax liability instead of treating it as adjustable credit)

explanation.text: The Logic: Investment 1 (Equity MF LTCG): Taxable = Rs. 3,00,000 - Rs. 1,25,000 exemption = Rs. 1,75,000. Tax = 1,75,000 x 12.5% = Rs. 21,875. Cess = Rs. 875. Total = Rs. 22,750. Investment 2 (Debt MF, purchased Feb 2024 - post April 2023): ALL gains at slab rate. Tax = 50,000 x 30% = Rs. 15,000. Cess = Rs. 600. Total = Rs. 15,600. Investment 3 (ELSS LTCG, equity-oriented): Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption already fully consumed by Investment 1. Tax = 80,000 x 12.5% = Rs. 10,000. Cess = Rs. 400. Total = Rs. 10,400. Investment 4 (IDCW): Rs. 8,000 at 30% slab = Rs. 2,400. Cess = Rs. 96. Total tax = Rs. 2,496. TDS of 10% x Rs. 8,000 = Rs. 800 (since IDCW > Rs. 5,000) is deducted and available as credit. Grand Total Tax Liability = Rs. 22,750 + Rs. 15,600 + Rs. 10,400 + Rs. 2,496 = Rs. 51,246. TDS credit available = Rs. 800 (adjustable when filing ITR, but total TAX LIABILITY remains Rs. 51,246). The Trap: Option A uses the pre-revision 10% LTCG rate and old Rs. 1 lakh exemption. Option C arrives at the correct pre-cess figure but forgets to add the 4% health and education cess. Option D subtracts TDS from the tax liability — TDS is a credit against tax due, but the total tax computed remains Rs. 51,246. Note: The cited workbook (NISM V-A, pp.155-162) supports the broad taxation framework, ELSS classification, IDCW TDS, STT, holding periods, and the Rs. 1.25 lakh equity LTCG exemption, but the explicit 12.5% LTCG rate, the post-April-2023 slab-rate treatment of debt funds, and the 4% cess are not stated on those pages (p.156 footnote refers candidates to AMFI tax-regime material). The rate, cess, and debt-fund treatment used in the calculation reflect general current Income Tax Act treatment.
